strengths: Strong empirical results (89.6 PDMS on NAVSIM), surpassing prior vision-only SOTA by 5.6 points with compelling ablation studies demonstrating contribution of each component
Substantial dataset contribution of 3.1M high-quality driving QA pairs with thorough data processing pipeline (normalization, filtering, augmentation) and automatic annotation infrastructure

Well-motivated three-stage training paradigm that systematically addresses identified limitations: domain gap through driving pre-training, language-to-action mismatch via diffusion planner, and imitation learning suboptimality through RL
Comprehensive experimental evaluation including scaling laws, hyperparameter sensitivity analysis, and extended metrics demonstrating broad capability across multiple performance dimensions
Reproducibility: detailed hyperparameters, dataset descriptions, and implementation details facilitate reproduction and build upon this work
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: combines established components (VLMs for driving, diffusion policies, RL) primarily representing engineering integration rather than fundamental methodological advances
Single-dataset evaluation on NAVSIM non-reactive simulator limits generalization claims and doesn't capture interactive driving scenarios critical for real deployment; no real-world validation

Unfair baseline comparisons: reproduced VLM baselines trained only on NAVSIM trajectories lacking the 3.1M QA pair pre-training that ReCogDrive receives; missing direct comparisons with cited VLM methods (DriveVLM, EMMA, OmniDrive, Agency-Driver)
Critical design choice not justified: diffusion planner vs. directly predicting from VLM outputs never compared; VLM freezing during stages 2-3 limits potential end-to-end optimization
Claimed 'autoregressive output collapse' lacks quantitative evidence; no error analysis or concrete examples comparing VLM-only trajectories with proposed method on identical scenarios
Computational overhead not addressed: training requires 32 GPUs, 'relatively high inference latency' mentioned but no concrete numbers; no computational cost comparison with baselines
Statistical rigor absent: no error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests; appears to be single-run results without multiple random seeds or multiple evaluation runs

Heavy reliance on automatic annotation using Qwen2.5-VL for filtering (quality score <60 removed) introduces potential circular dependency; 0.8M of 3.2M pairs filtered away with unclear quality implications; no inter-annotator agreement validation
